adulate

AJ-oo-layt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To adulate is to praise someone excessively and fawningly.

The courtiers would adulate the young prince's every decision, however small.

Worked Example

Employees who wanted to get ahead learned to adulate their notoriously vain manager at every meeting.

Adulate describes fawning, often insincere praise heaped on someone who holds power over the person doing the praising.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

flatter: To flatter is to praise someone a little more than they deserve, often to get on their good side, and one smooth compliment is enough to do it. To adulate goes much further: constant, gushing, over-the-top praise that never lets up. Flattery is a small tactic; adulation is nonstop fawning.

kowtow to: To kowtow to someone is to give in to them and obey, bowing to their every wish -- you can kowtow silently, just by never pushing back. To adulate is specifically about praise: heaping loud, excessive compliments on the person. Kowtowing is surrender; adulating is flattery turned up to worship.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

criticize: express disapproval of

condemn: express strong disapproval of

Where it sits · how excessive the praise becomes — compliment → adulate → grovel

compliment vs. adulate: Complimenting someone is a normal, healthy form of praise; adulating them crosses into fawning excess.

grovel vs. adulate: To grovel is to abase yourself completely before someone, a step beyond simply adulating them.

The pieces

root — adul

root — adul: to fawn on (Latin (adulari))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to cause to become (Latin (-are))

Put it together

Put it together: adul ("to fawn on") + -ate ("to make") = to fawn on with excessive praise.
